AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim in substance. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from `__init__` (turret_operator.py:74-76). The game applies it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded inside StartCombatInternal, i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart; the sim runs it at create_monsters (combat.py:241, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :134), before relics attach (combat.py:274, was :157-159), before belt potions register (bare filename, was :164-166), before the parity Niche HP roll (combat.py:266-269, was :152-153) and before hooks.on_combat_start (combat.py:356, was :208). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the four ported listeners on the reachable hooks (relics/ruined_helmet.py, relics/unsettling_lamp.py, relics/vambrace.py, relics/paels_legion.py) all gate on the player or on a non-null card and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card; (b) HP-roll inversion -- of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp, and only inside revive() (powers.py:2063, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :1581, logic unchanged); (c) roll ordering -- EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` prints `living_shield  sticky-no-op   initial=SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE (MoveState)`, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the constructor's first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Rule 7: the four relic files and powers.py are cited by name here and are NOT all hashed by this record. Amount checked: LivingShield.cs:35 applies 25m and _RAMPART_BLOCK is 25 (turret_operator.py:24). ESCALATION CHECK, because SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 requires one whenever the unit's graph reads combat state: LivingShield's ConditionalBranchState condition calls `_ally_count`, which reads `self._hooks.combat.enemies` (turret_operator.py:78-84) -- and that attribute does NOT exist yet during create_monsters (the assignment at combat.py:241, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :134, has not completed). The condition is nevertheless never evaluated during construction, and that is EXECUTED, not assumed: `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` prints `living_shield sticky-no-op initial=SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE (MoveState)`, i.e. monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires on the constructor's roll, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b08.py graphs` builds the monster without an AttributeError. RampartPower's own behaviour is audit/records/power/rampart.json's, not re-verdicted here.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: LivingShield.cs:38-52 node for node: SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE (6) -> SHIELD_SLAM_BRANCH, a ConditionalBranchState with AddState(SHIELD_SLAM, () => GetAllyCount() > 0) then AddState(SMASH, () => GetAllyCount() == 0); SMASH_MOVE (16 + 3 Strength) -> ITSELF, so once the escort is dead the Living Shield smashes and enrages every turn with no path back. Initial state SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE. EXECUTED (`graphs` and `ally-count`): the sim prints `SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE -> SHIELD_SLAM_BRANCH`, `SMASH_MOVE -> SMASH_MOVE`, `COND SHIELD_SLAM_BRANCH order=['SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE', 'SMASH_MOVE']`, initial=SHIELD_SLAM_MOVE. The dispatcher is a ConditionalBranchState, whose AddState takes no integer arguments at all (ConditionalBranchState.cs:10-23), so bug class 6 / monster_state_machine G1 cannot apply to this unit. Numbers: ShieldSlamDamage literal 6 (no ascension helper), SmashDamage GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 18, 16) = 16, EnrageStr literal 3.

guards.what: GetAllyCount (LivingShield.cs:71-74) vs the sim's _ally_count -- two different filters that must agree
guards.rationale: C# is `CombatState.GetTeammatesOf(Creature).Count(c => c.IsAlive && c != Creature)`; GetTeammatesOf is GetCreaturesOnSide(creature.Side) and INCLUDES the creature itself (CombatState.cs:394-400), which is what the `c != Creature` term is for, and IsAlive is `CurrentHp > 0` (Creature.cs:206). The sim is `sum(1 for c in combat.enemies if c is not self and not c.is_gone)` (turret_operator.py:78-84), where is_gone is `is_dead or escaped` and is_dead is `hp <= 0` (creatures.py:173-179, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :40-46, same properties moved). The two filters differ in wording and agree in every reachable state, EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b08.py ally-count`): both alive -> 1; the Turret Operator at 0 HP -> 0; and -- the case the wordings could have parted on -- the Turret Operator at 0 HP with retained_after_death=True (a corpse the combat deliberately KEEPS in `enemies`, SHARED-FINDINGS section 7's death-is-not-removal shape) -> still 0, because is_gone tests HP and not membership. C# reaches the same answer for the same reason: a retained corpse is still in Enemies and still fails IsAlive. The `escaped` term is the sim's only extra, and it is the sim's way of expressing what C# expresses by REMOVING the creature from Enemies (CreatureCmd.Escape), so it is the same filter. Note the condition is evaluated at ROLL time, not at construction -- see the AfterAddedToRoom entry's escalation check.

guards.what: Conditional branch add order and the C# throw when nothing matches
guards.rationale: C# adds SHIELD_SLAM first, SMASH second (LivingShield.cs:45-46); the sim adds them in the same order (turret_operator.py:96-97), and GetNextState returns the first branch whose Evaluate() > 0 (ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54 / state_machine.py:228-232). The two predicates (> 0 and == 0) partition the integers, so the `throw`/`raise` arm is dead on both sides -- consistent with monster_state_machine N3, which is not re-verdicted here.

guards.what: SmashMove's order: damage first, then the +3 Strength
guards.rationale: LivingShield.cs:62-69 attacks for 16 and THEN applies StrengthPower(3) to itself, so the Nth Smash hits for 16 + 3*(N-1) and not 16 + 3*N. turret_operator.py:105-109 has the same order. The +3 is applied with applier: Creature in C# and with the default in the sim, which matters only to applier-keyed listeners and StrengthPower has none here.

monsters/base.py:338-349 (re-verified 2026-08-04, was :107-118) `_execute_attack` fires before_attack, loops `hits` times through DamageCmd.deal and breaks when the player or the attacker is dead; then after_attack. C#'s AttackCommand.Execute (AttackCommand.cs:528-546) has the same two loop guards -- `if (Attacker.IsDead) break;` and an empty alive-target list -- and the sim's single target IS the player, so the two loops agree hit for hit. The one asymmetry is C#'s PRE-loop `if (Attacker.IsDead) return this;` (AttackCommand.cs:528-531), which also skips Hook.BeforeAttack; the sim has no such pre-guard. Unreachable for this unit and EXECUTED rather than asserted (rule 5): a sim monster can only take a turn while dead if `retained_after_death` is set (bare filename, was combat.py:292, :306; re-verified 2026-08-04 the same is_gone/retained_after_death gate still exists, moved), that flag is written only where hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death returns False (bare filename, was cmds.py:102-104, :200-202), and `grep -rn 'def should_remove_from_combat_after_death' sts2_rl/` returns exactly two sites -- the hook itself (hooks.py:1892, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :603) and ReattachPower (bare filename, was powers.py:2338), which this monster never holds.
